prompt:
One of our legacy partners sends us data in a pipe-delimited text format that isn't quite CSV -- it uses backslash escapes instead of quoting, so Python's `csv` module can't read or write it directly. Please add a `pipedelim.py` module (standard library only) at the project root implementing it:

- `parse_records(text)` -> parses the whole text into a list of records, where each record is a list of field strings.
- `format_records(records)` -> the inverse: serializes a list of records (each a list of field strings) back into text.
- `PipeFormatError` -> a `ValueError` subclass raised when text passed to `parse_records` is malformed.

Format rules:

- Records are separated by a real newline character (`\n`). Fields within a record are separated by a real pipe character (`|`).
- To put a literal `|`, a literal `\`, or a literal newline *inside* a field's value, it must be written as the two-character escape sequence `\|`, `\\`, or `\n` respectively (backslash followed by one of those three characters). A backslash followed by anything else is invalid. A backslash as the very last character of a record (nothing after it to escape) is invalid. Both of these raise `PipeFormatError`. No other characters are ever escaped.
- `parse_records("")` (a completely empty string) returns `[]` -- zero records, not one. Every other text represents at least one record: a lone `\n` is one record containing a single empty field (`[['']]`), because real newlines and pipes are always separators, and the only way a record or field can be "empty" is to have nothing between its surrounding separators (or start/end of text). A text that ends with `\n` has that final newline treated as a terminator for the last record, not as introducing a new empty record after it -- but an interior blank line (two newlines in a row) is a genuine empty record, same as in ordinary line-based text formats.
- `parse_records` raises `TypeError` if `text` is not a `str`.

`format_records(records)` rules:

- `records` must be a `list` or `tuple`; each record in it must be a `list` or `tuple` of `str` fields. Anything else raises `TypeError` (fields are never auto-converted to `str` -- callers must pass strings).
- Every record must have at least one field; an empty record (`[]`) raises `PipeFormatError`, since there's no way to write a zero-field record in this format.
- Escape each field's `\`, `|`, and real newline characters as described above (escape backslashes themselves before introducing any new backslashes from escaping `|` or newline -- otherwise you'll double-escape).
- `format_records([])` (zero records) returns the empty string `""`. Otherwise, join the escaped records with `\n` and add exactly one trailing `\n` at the end. This trailing newline matters: it's what makes `format_records([['']])` (one record, one empty field) produce `"\n"`, which is different from `format_records([])` producing `""` -- without it, those two very different inputs would produce the same output and `parse_records` could never tell them apart.
- For any valid `records` value, `parse_records(format_records(records))` must equal `records` again.

A few basic tests are sketched in `tests/test_pipedelim.py`.
